name: festival-sunset-figure
prompt: Vertical phone snapshot from a summer music festival in 2016, the last ten minutes before the sun drops behind the trees. A grassy field trampled flat, warm haze kicked up from the ground, strings of round bulb lights looped between wooden poles overhead and just switching on. Paper confetti in pink, gold and teal hangs in the air, caught mid-fall. In the foreground and background a happy crowd seen only from behind and well out of focus: soft shapes of shoulders, raised arms, a few heads wearing crowns of fake daisies and roses, no faces turned toward us. Dead centre in the middle distance, the only thing in crisp focus, stands a single figure facing straight into the lens, completely still, arms down, one gloved hand holding a lit sparkler that throws a small white spray of sparks. The figure wears a plain dark knitted balaclava with no eye, nose or mouth openings at all, so no skin shows anywhere; a large white ring is stitched around the whole face, and one small red triangle with softly rounded corners, point downward, sits high inside the ring toward the right side of the picture. Dark gloves, dark plain clothes, no skin, no machinery. Shot on an older phone camera at roughly head height, slight wide-angle, the low sun just off the right edge of the frame blowing a big orange and magenta lens flare with hexagon ghosts across the crowd. The whole image carries a heavy oversaturated warm photo filter of that era: lifted faded blacks, pushed oranges and pinks, a rosy cast over everything, mild grain and a soft vignette. Joyful blur everywhere, one motionless sharp figure in the middle of it. No text, no logos, no signage, no lettering anywhere in the image. Thanks.
